issues.legal_issue: A plaint amendment that assists in determining the real controversy and does not change the nature of the suit may be allowed without deciding the merits of the amended claim at the amendment stage.
material_facts: The suit, which sought eviction and mesne profits or damages, had been restored after the ex parte decree was set aside.
The plaintiff sought to delete a separate claim for delivery of air tickets and include their value with the claim for mesne profits, together with a consequential amendment.
The proposed amendment concerned the amount of mesne profits or damages and relied on contractual rent and the value of a benefit received through letting the premises.
The courts below rejected the amendment, including on the view that contractual charges were not relevant to determining mesne profits.
The Supreme Court found the amendment necessary to determine the real controversy over the quantum of mesne profits or damages and found that it would not change the nature of the suit.
issues.conclusion: The orders refusing the amendment were set aside and the amendment was allowed. The plaintiff could plead and prove the contractual rent and the equivalent benefit received, while the merits of the claim remained for decision at trial.
issues.legal_principle: An amendment may be allowed when it is necessary to adjudicate the real controversy and does not change the nature of the suit. At the amendment stage, the court must not decide the merits of the claim, which are to be determined when the suit is decided. A plaintiff may plead and prove contractual rent and the equivalent benefit received from letting the property in support of a mesne-profits or damages claim; on the lease agreement in this case, such damages could not be less than the contractual rate of use and occupation charges. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for these principles.

rule.if: plaint_amendment_application and suit_restored_for_trial and amendment_addresses_mesne_profit_quantum and amendment_adds_contractual_use_value and amendment_does_not_change_suit_nature

predicates.plaint_amendment_application: A party applied to change the pleading in a pending civil suit.
predicates.suit_restored_for_trial: The suit was returned to the trial process after an earlier ex parte decree was set aside.
predicates.amendment_addresses_mesne_profit_quantum: The proposed change concerned the amount of mesne profits or damages in dispute.
predicates.amendment_adds_contractual_use_value: The proposed change included contractual rent or the value of a contractual benefit in the mesne-profits or damages claim.
predicates.amendment_does_not_change_suit_nature: The proposed change left the essential nature of the suit unchanged.

issues.definition: When a party seeks a pleading change in a restored suit, the change addresses the disputed amount and adds contractual use value without changing the suit's nature, the change is allowed.
